claim: AlphaEvolve, an evolutionary coding agent orchestrating a pipeline of LLMs that continuously receives feedback from one or more evaluators, iteratively improves algorithms and achieved a 56-year-first improvement over Strassen's algorithm for 4x4 complex matrix multiplication (48 scalar multiplications).
stance_target: Blanket claim that iterative performance feedback degrades LLM-guided architecture/program search proposals
scope_conditions: Program/algorithm discovery at Google/DeepMind, frontier LLMs, multi-evaluator population-based evolutionary loop
quoted_support: Using an evolutionary approach, continuously receiving feedback from one or more evaluators, AlphaEvolve iteratively improves the algorithm... AlphaEvolve developed a search algorithm that found a procedure to multiply two 4x4 complex-valued matrices using 48 scalar multiplications; offering the first improvement, after 56 years, over Strassen's algorithm in this setting.

claim: AlphaEvolve applied to Google's computational infrastructure produced a more efficient data-center scheduling algorithm, a simplification in TPU hardware accelerator circuit design, and accelerated training of the LLM underpinning AlphaEvolve itself, all via iterative LLM-driven evolutionary feedback loops.
stance_target: That iterative feedback cannot improve real-world engineering/architecture search outcomes
quoted_support: AlphaEvolve developed a more efficient scheduling algorithm for data centers, found a functionally equivalent simplification in the circuit design of hardware accelerators, and accelerated the training of the LLM underpinning AlphaEvolve itself.

claim: AlphaEvolve explicitly extends prior automated discovery methods from Romera-Paredes et al. 2023 (FunSearch), situating iterative LLM+evaluator feedback loops as a maturing, incrementally-improving research lineage rather than a one-off result.
stance_target: Novelty and lineage of iterative-feedback LLM search methods
quoted_support: significantly expanding the scope of prior automated discovery methods (Romera-Paredes et al., 2023).

claim: AlphaEvolve's positive iterative-feedback results come from a large-scale, frontier-model, multi-evaluator, population-based evolutionary system, not a single small quantized model refining proposals sequentially within one context -- a scale/architecture confound that bounds rather than defeats a narrower 'small single-model self-refinement degrades proposals' claim.
stance_target: Whether AlphaEvolve's success defeats, bounds, or is orthogonal to the target paper's thesis
scope_conditions: Comparison of system architectures: AlphaEvolve (multi-LLM, population-based, external evaluators) vs. small single-model sequential self-refinement
quoted_support: AlphaEvolve orchestrates an autonomous pipeline of LLMs, whose task is to improve an algorithm by making direct changes to the code.
